claim: Luminal proteins assemble into a chitinous central rod and into a cuticular apical extracellular matrix (aECM, taenidia), lining the apical membrane
source: Luminal proteins assemble into a chitinous central rod and into a cuticular apical extracellular matrix (aECM, taenidia), lining the apical membrane.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and is based on established knowledge about tracheal development.

claim: After 10 hr, luminal material becomes rapidly cleared from the tubes by massive endocytosis involving several endocytic pathways
source: After 10 hr, luminal material becomes rapidly cleared from the tubes by massive endocytosis involving several endocytic pathways.

claim: A liquid clearance pulse converts the tubes into functional airways

claim: Tube elongation is continuous during tracheal development

claim: Tube elongation termination requires chitin biosynthesis and the secreted chitin deacetylases vermiform (Verm) and serpentine (Serp)
source: Tube elongation is continuous during tracheal development and its termination requires chitin biosynthesis and the secreted chitin deacetylases vermiform (Verm) and serpentine (Serp) (Beitel and Krasnow, 2000; Luschnig et al., 2006; Wang et al., 2006; Öztürk-Çolak et al., 2016).

claim: Luminal proteins presumably modify the structure and physical properties of the aECM and thereby restrict tube elongation
source: These luminal proteins presumably modify the structure and physical properties of the aECM and thereby restrict tube elongation.

claim: Components involved in the assembly of basolateral septate junctions (SJs) restrict tube elongation through the regulation of the subcellular localization of Crumbs (Crb)
source: In addition to the luminal matrix pathway, components involved in the assembly of basolateral septate junctions (SJs) also restrict tube elongation, through the regulation of the subcellular localization of Crumbs (Crb), a transmembrane protein that promotes expansion of the tracheal cell apical surface and tube elongation (Laprise et al., 2010).

claim: Crumbs (Crb) is a transmembrane protein that promotes expansion of the tracheal cell apical surface and tube elongation
source: In addition to the luminal matrix pathway, components involved in the assembly of basolateral septate junctions (SJs) also restrict tube elongation, through the regulation of the subcellular localization of Crumbs (Crb), a transmembrane protein that promotes expansion of the tracheal cell apical surface and tube elongation (Laprise et al., 2010).

claim: Src oncogene at 42A (Src42A) promotes axial elongation by controlling the apical cytoskeleton and apical cell

evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Yorkie (Yki) and several components of the Hippo pathway control tube elongation
source: Additionally, Yorkie (Yki) and several components of the Hippo pathway control tube elongation, along with transcription factors like Blimp-1 and Grainy head (Grh) (Hemphälä et al., 2003; Robbins et al., 2014; Öztürk-Çolak et al., 2016; McSharry and Beitel, 2019; Skouloudaki et al., 2019).

claim: Transcription factors like Blimp-1 and Grainy head (Grh) control tube elongation
source: Additionally, Yorkie (Yki) and several components of the Hippo pathway control tube elongation, along with transcription factors like Blimp-1 and Grainy head (Grh) (Hemphälä et al., 2003; Robbins et al., 2014; Öztürk-Çolak et al., 2016; McSharry and Beitel, 2019; Skouloudaki et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

source: Cluster of differentiation 36 (CD36) belongs to class B scavenger receptor family, which includes scavenger receptor B1 (SRB1) and lysosomal integral membrane protein 2 (LIMP2).

claim: CD36 has several cargoes, including long-chain fatty acids, oxidized LDL (ox-LDL), oxidized phospholipids and thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1)
source: CD36 has several cargoes, including long-chain fatty acids, oxidized LDL (ox-LDL), oxidized phospholipids and thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1) (Githaka et al., 2016; Deng et al., 2022).

claim: CD36 clustering at the cell surface upon engagement of multivalent ligands and in conjunction with the cortical cytoskeleton triggers signal transduction and receptor–ligand complex endocytosis

source: The Drosophila genome includes a family of 14 CD36-like genes, with distinct tissue-specific expression patterns.

source: The genetic analysis of a few members in this class B scavenger receptor family implicated them in phagocytosis, immune responses, and photoreceptor function (Philips et al., 2005; Stuart et al., 2005; Voolstra et al., 2006).

source: Reduction of Src42A in emp mutants, rescues the tube elongation phenotype indicating that Emp modulates junctional p-Src42A levels to control apical membrane expansion and tube length.

claim: Emp provides a direct link between ECM, apical membrane, and cytoskeleton during tube maturation process
source: Emp binds to βH-Spectrin directly, suggesting that it provides a direct link between ECM, apical membrane, and cytoskeleton during tube maturation process.

source: Re-expression of human CD36 in emp mutants can ameliorate the mutant tube phenotypes suggesting conserved functions of Emp.

source: The survival of emp mutants overexpressing emp in the airways was limited to larval stages, suggesting that the tracheal-specific re-expression of emp is not sufficient for larval or adult survival.

claim: Emp has additional roles in other tissues beyond the trachea
source: This suggests additional roles for Emp in other tissues.
